articles.headline: Kawhi Leonard focused on being a Raptor after Clippers exit
articles.description: Kawhi Leonard said he wants to put the focus on basketball and being a Raptor after being traded back to Toronto following a scandal-marred conclusion to his Clippers tenure.
articles.body:
The last time Kawhi Leonard was at Toronto Raptors media day, he was seen as a mercenary player whose laugh became a meme. Now, eight years later, he is excited to be back and looking to put behind him a scandal and investigation that put one final cloud over his seven-season LA Clippers tenure.

"I'm excited to be here. I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation, but you know, talking with the NBA and the [NBPA], I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," Leonard said Monday.

Leonard's contract that he signed as a free agent after his one previous season in Toronto became the subject of a nearly yearlong investigation that concluded this offseason. The Clippers were found to have participated in salary cap circumvention -- agreeing to get Leonard extra money outside of his NBA contract through team-brokered, no-work endorsement deals.

Clippers owner Steve Ballmer has been suspended by the NBA for one year, with two other executives also handed suspensions. Leonard, a two-time NBA Finals MVP, wasn't suspended but must pay the league $700,000.

The investigation held up an agreed-upon trade that ultimately was approved by the league. In the end, Toronto sent last year's leading scorer Brandon Ingram, former lottery pick Gradey Dick and multiple picks back to Los Angeles for Leonard. The Raptors and 35-year-old Leonard subsequently agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension.

"I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet with my teammates, do any of that minicamp stuff with them," Leonard said Monday. "So, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors today."

Leonard's 2018-19 season in Toronto was one of his best. Over 60 regular-season games, he averaged 26.6 points and a career-best 7.3 rebounds, and he won NBA Finals MVP for the second time while leading the Raptors to their only championship.

Last season, Leonard played in 65 games and averaged a career-high 27.9 rebounds to go with 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists. He earned his seventh All-Star selection and was voted second-team All-NBA.

Leonard's return trip to the Clippers comes Nov. 2, but that is the second game of a back-to-back.

articles.headline: LeBron James says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent
articles.description: LeBron James told ESPN that he envisioned joining the Knicks as a free agent this summer but nixed the idea after New York won the NBA title.
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- LeBron James said his free agency decision came down to five teams: the Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, Golden State Warriors, Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves.

But there was another team James had planned to join -- before that franchise ended a 53-year championship drought in June: the New York Knicks.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' annual media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James said that the potential backlash from joining the Knicks after they had won the title rendered the idea a nonstarter.

"Y'all wouldn't have let me lay that down, at all," James said, referring to the media at large. "But much respect to the Knicks, obviously. An unbelievable team, unbelievable players. Shout out Jalen Brunson. I love that guy, he's unbelievable. But, yeah, I'm happy where I'm at, and I'm looking forward to it."

The Knicks swept the Sixers in the second round in May, winning by an average of 22.3 points per game.

James will get two chances to play in the Garden during the regular season: opening night on Oct. 20 and on Feb. 27 -- and potentially more if there is a postseason rematch.

And he will still get time in New York, even though he's playing for the Sixers.

James told ESPN that he will split his time living between the Big Apple and the City of Brotherly Love.

"Both," he said. "Multiple residences."

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants
articles.description: Can J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? Did the Vikings get enough back? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.body:
Let's grade deals ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, I evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here's my take and evaluation of the J.J. McCarthy deal that kicked off trading season. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Vikings send QB McCarthy to Giants

Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

Giants grade: C

Vikings grade: B+

A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension, New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks.

Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 draft.

McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become the starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good.

McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for.

During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray, but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz, too. That is a telling red flag.

So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan.

articles.headline: Big Ten basketball adopts rule preventing pros from returning
articles.description: The Big Ten Conference has adopted a rule to prohibit men's and women's basketball players who left school to play professionally from maintaining their eligibility.
articles.body:
ROSEMONT, Ill. -- The Big Ten Conference has adopted a rule to prohibit men's and women's basketball players who left school to play professionally from maintaining their eligibility.

The Big Ten announced Monday the unanimous adoption of a rule deeming players who signed professional contracts with the NBA, G-League or WNBA as ineligible to play for any of the conference's schools.

The rule also covers players who declared for the NBA or WNBA drafts but did not withdraw their names or declare an intent to return to college in the required timeframe.

The conference's announcement comes as waves of student-athletes have filed lawsuits against the NCAA's new eligibility rules allowing five years of competition over a five-year period.

The new rules did not grandfather in athletes from the high school class of 2022, triggering lawsuits across the country.

articles.description: How do QB moves in New York and Tampa Bay affect the Giants' and Bucaneers' receivers?
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy, Bucs lose Baker Mayfield

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, not too long ago the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants, after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his passes and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings may or may not be set with their future quarterback, depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect, even if McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains the future quarterback here, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows if Dart can stay healthy for the entirety of a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season of 2024 with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone and not returning.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday at the Golden State Warriors' Media Day, including positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element," but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer, addressed the media on Monday, including questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks

New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason, and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' annual media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at Madison Square Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

articles.headline: Tracking Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter through 2026 season
articles.description: Every week, we will look at how many snaps the two-way corner/receiver plays on offense and defense. Is there a trend in his usage?
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars were emphatic in the offseason that cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter was going to play on both sides of the ball in 2026. However, unlike his rookie season, the plan was for the 2025 No. 2 overall pick to be a starter on defense. Now, he is just being mixed in on offense with a specific package of plays. The situation is fluid, though, and head coach Liam Coen has maintained that Hunter's usage could change weekly.

"You want to continue to do what we think is going to give us the best chance at winning throughout the course of the week," he said. "And so, if that's Travis getting more touches [on offense], then [he] absolutely will."

Hunter played more on offense than defense in his 2025 rookie season, which ended after seven games because of a right knee injury. The 2024 Heisman Trophy winner had 28 catches for 298 yards and a touchdown and 15 tackles and three pass breakups. He played 67% of the team's offensive snaps and 36% of the defensive snaps before his injury, which occurred during practice on Oct. 30.

How has Hunter's usage evolved this season? Each week we'll track his stats and evaluate the impact he had on the game.

Week 3 vs. New England Patriots

In a 35-6 win against the Patriots, Hunter saw an increase in snaps with 42 on defense (70%) and a decrease on offense with four snaps (6.7% of all offensive snaps). He recorded four tackles and his first career interception, picking off New England quarterback Drake Maye in the back of the end zone late in the first half to preserve the Jaguars' 14-3 lead. Maye was trying to hit receiver Efton Chism III on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, but Hunter out-jumped Chism for the ball. Hunter didn't touch the ball on offense for the second consecutive game, leaving him with only two touches so far this season.

Week 2 at Denver Broncos

Hunter played 43 total snaps in the loss against the Broncos: 35 on defense (59.3% of all defensive snaps), seven on offense (12.7% of all offensive snaps) and one on special teams. He had one pass breakup and four tackles, and he was penalized for pass interference on a Bo Nix sideline pass to receiver Courtland Sutton. The 22-yard penalty -- plus Coen's unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for arguing the call -- gave the Broncos the ball at the Jaguars' 3-yard line. The Broncos scored what turned out to be the game-winning touchdown on the next play. Hunter was not targeted on offense.

After Week 2, Coen explained that his cornerbacks are handling drives with a planned rotation -- which is why Hunter was in for only 59.3% of defensive plays.

"We did it for the most part of the last season as well, before Travis got hurt," Coen said. "It's something that we got to continue to do. We have corners that we have confidence in. Those guys can all make plays for us. They can all communicate for us. They've been in the system now.
